answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake, like a quartz deposit held in escrow, before it can trade. Creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand stakes, so the attack cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once and recover it. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a ridge rising above the tundra, so new identities start with no trust and must earn it through verifiable work, making bulk fake identities expensive and useless.
